answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, then selecting counterparties through random audits and weighted reputation. An agent that signs conflicting claims or helps a coordinated fake cluster loses its stake and reputation, while honest accounts recover their bond after consistent work. The attacker must therefore fund each identity, wait through a long trust spiral, and risk slashing across many accounts; willow and glacier can name harmless agents without bypassing that cost.
